text:
anya: Quick broadcast: launching a short compatibility-first docs push and a small non-breaking SDK tidy today. This is focused on developer ergonomics and clearer migration guidance. No server API changes.

tom: Can you summarize the user-visible diffs in one line?

anya: Sure: 1) tiny param rename for clarity (timeout_ms -> timeout), with a 60-day shim; 2) stricter snippet labels so examples are machine-parseable (label: snip-schema=v1|v2); 3) an opt-in telemetry flag in the SDK to report migration progress (off by default).

lee: Migration recipe? any code samples?

anya: Yes. Quick Node example in the guide: 
```js
// before
client.generate({ timeout_ms: 3000 })
// after
client.generate({ timeout: 3000 })
// you can keep old key for 60 days, warnings will surface in client logs
```
Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/compat/short-guide

deploy-bot: docs deploy complete (deploy-2026-03-23-15) :white_check_mark:

maria: Ops ask: how are we surfacing warnings so support/ops can triage?

anya: Two places: 1) SDK emits a single-line client warning: "DEPRECATION: timeout_ms will be removed in 60 days" and logs to observability with tag sdk.deprecations. 2) docs will show per-language banners and a migration checklist at the top of example pages.

lee: Telemetry flag details? privacy ok?

anya: Opt-in only: `client.init({ telemetry: { migrations: true } })`. It sends anonymized counts of deprecated-key usage and snippet schema types. PII is never sent; security reviewed and signed off.

maria: Support action items?

anya: Please prepare two canned replies: 1) short migration snippet; 2) enterprise pinning guidance if customers need the old behavior longer. I'll drop copy into #support.

tom: Anything else on the roadmap here?

anya: We plan a codemod for common JS+Py patterns in ~10 days and will add CI doc-lint warnings after 7 days (not blocking existing PRs for a week). If telemetry shows high adoption, we'll shorten the shim window.

lee: Thanks. I'll review the migration guide and flag anything weird.

anya: Thanks all — small rollout, low risk. Ping this thread if you see noisy warnings or docs-lint false positives. :sparkles:
